SOURCING, FROM FIRST PRINCIPLES

The job: "what do I need to push on right now?" Stage is a property of a row, not the layout.

What changed and why:
· The five-lane board is gone. Listed already had to be special-cased into a searchable list inside a lane, because it grows without bound — a lane that is not a lane means the kanban was wrong for this data.
· The five stage colours (#818E9B … #11402E) are gone. They were outside the 23-value palette and, at a glance, four of them read as the same dark green. Position is now five segments of ink: past, here, ahead.
· One accent. The oxide edge marks NEEDS YOU and nothing else on the screen.

THE FIGURE THE PAGE NEVER HAD

Sourcing decides whether to stock something, and the old screen showed no money at all.

"Cost to bring in" is the cash the asked-for quantity would tie up, at the cheapest price found — derived, never invented, and it carries its own basis: on the 2 items of 8 that have a price. The other six say "no price yet", not zero.

ASKS vs ASKERS

Five asks from one builder is not the signal five customers are. Every row keeps both: the figure is different people, the basis line says how many asks.

The test suite pins this in both directions; the design must not quietly collapse it into one counter.

820px is a SWITCH, not a reflow.

No stepper scrubber, no horizontal scroll, no drag-to-pan — the phone gets a plain list of what needs you, actions visible at 44px rather than behind an eye icon, 15px body.
"Not enough is an answer." The strip stays, at zero, so the empty screen teaches the shape of the full one; the copy names the three doors that fill it and says dropped items are kept, never deleted.
